hook: Test six made-up pages twice: call each one from the page alone, then leave it and see what the rest of the web says.
outcome: Judge a source by reading laterally: ask who is behind it, what the evidence is and what other sources say, and see in your own data how often the page alone fooled you
sources: AASL, National School Library Standards (2018), Standards Framework for Learners: Curate IV.B.3, Engage VI.A.3: https://standards.aasl.org/framework/
Wineburg, S. and McGrew, S. (2019). Lateral Reading and the Nature of Expertise: Reading Less and Learning More When Evaluating Digital Information. Teachers College Record 121(11)
Digital Inquiry Group (formerly Stanford History Education Group), Civic Online Reasoning: Who's behind the information? What's the evidence? What do other sources say? https://cor.inquirygroup.org/
ICANN Registration Data Lookup (what a domain lookup shows): https://lookup.icann.org/
National Park Service, Denali National Park, Amphibians (wood frogs freeze solid in winter and thaw in spring): https://www.nps.gov/dena/learn/nature/amphibians.htm
Reserved example domains, RFC 2606 and RFC 6761: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2606
All specimens, sites, people, studies and organizations are made up for Curio Class; the verdict match rule and the three-verdict scale are the tool's own
Photos generated with FLUX (no people); browser, pages, logos, avatars, jars and the table drawn in code
